strategy.summary: CART-31 reports two cartTotal mispricings in src/cart.js. (1) bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (src/cart.js:22) though BULK_THRESHOLD's doc says "at least this many", so 10 items at $10 is charged $100 instead of $90. (2) A $3 cart with SAVE5 should cost $4.99; reading the code, cartTotal already clamps goods with Math.max(0, …) (line 31), so this symptom is expected not to reproduce — the test will assert the ticket's $4.99 and report whatever it shows.
inScope: cartTotal bulk discount at exactly 10 items
cartTotal with SAVE5 on a cart cheaper than the coupon
assumptions: Prices are plain dollar numbers as in the existing test (price, quantity lines).
The 'at least 10 items' rule from the ticket and the BULK_THRESHOLD doc comment is the intended behaviour.
openQuestions: The SAVE5 negative-total report does not reproduce from reading the code (goods are clamped at 0); was the customer on an older version, or did the cart differ from '$3 with SAVE5'?

risks.description: An it.fails reproduction is the only test of the bulk discount, so a regression elsewhere in the discount would stay green
risks.mitigation: TC3 is a normal passing test that a multi-line cart of 11 items gets the 10% discount.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart holding 10 items in total (one line, quantity 10 at $10) gets the 10% bulk discount: cartTotal returns 90.
Goods never cost less than $0 after the SAVE5 coupon: a $3 cart with SAVE5 totals $4.99 (shipping only).
Carts above the bulk threshold, with quantities summed across lines, keep getting the bulk discount.

testCases.title: applies the bulk discount to a cart of exactly 10 items
testCases.expected: Returns 90; today fails with 'expected 100 to be 90' because bulkDiscount uses > instead of >= (src/cart.js:22).
testCases.rationale: Reproduces report 1 at the lowest level.

testCases.title: charges only shipping when SAVE5 exceeds a $3 cart
testCases.expected: Returns 4.99 (a negative total would be the reported symptom); expected to pass on current code since goods are clamped at 0.
testCases.testData: one line, price 3, quantity 1, coupon SAVE5
testCases.rationale: Reproduces report 2 with the ticket's data.

testCases.title: applies the bulk discount to 11 items spread over two lines
steps: Call cartTotal([{ price: 10, quantity: 5 }, { price: 10, quantity: 6 }])
testCases.rationale: Passing guard so the discount isn't covered only by an it.fails case.

strategy.environmentNotes: Pure unit tests; no services. Run with npm test (vitest run).

defects.title: No bulk discount at exactly 10 items
defects.description: AC1: a cart of 10 items at $10 should total $90 (10% bulk discount from 10 items, as BULK_THRESHOLD's doc says "at least this many"). bulkDiscount in src/cart.js:22 checks itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD instead of >=, so 10 items get no discount and the total is $100.
defects.evidence: AssertionError: expected 100 to be 90 // Object.is equality (test/cart-total.test.js:11)
